title: Analysis of sugar crystal size in honey
author: Weber, Meixner, et al.

steps.title: Weigh coverslip and honey
steps.instruction: Place a dry, fat‑free 18 mm coverslip on an analytical balance, tare it, then transfer 1.0 ± 0.2 mg honey onto the centre of the coverslip using a micro‑spatula.

steps.title: Mount coverslip in centrifuge
steps.instruction: Secure the coverslip in the converted smoothie‑maker (centrifuge) with the provided screws.

steps.title: Add polyethylene glycol
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of polyethylene glycol 200 onto the honey drop to lower the honey viscosity.

steps.title: Centrifuge briefly
steps.instruction: Within the next minute start the smoothie‑maker and centrifuge the sample for 20 seconds to spread the honey into a homogeneous film without overlapping crystals.

steps.title: Pre‑clean centrifuge chamber
steps.instruction: Before any sample, wipe the interior surface of the smoothie‑maker with a cotton swab moistened with distilled water, then place the swab in 3 mL distilled water for 10 minutes to dissolve any residual sugars.

steps.title: Post‑centrifugation cleaning
steps.instruction: After the honey has been centrifuged, repeat the cleaning: rub the interior with a fresh wetted cotton swab and soak the swab in 3 mL distilled water for 10 minutes before analysis.

steps.title: Prepare ion‑chromatography standards
steps.instruction: Prepare two standards in distilled water: one containing 1 mg L⁻¹ glucose and fructose, and a second containing 0.05 mg L⁻¹ fructose (the detection limit of the system).

steps.title: Run ion‑chromatography
steps.instruction: Inject the standards and the cotton‑swab extracts onto a Carbo‑PAC PA100 column (4 × 250 mm) using 100 mM sodium hydroxide as eluent at a flow rate of 1 mL min⁻¹. Detect with an amperometric cell equipped with a gold working electrode and a Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.

steps.title: Verify instrument sensitivity
steps.instruction: Confirm that the system sensitivity is 0.05 mg L⁻¹ for fructose, which is sufficient to detect a single fructose particle of 250 µm × 20 µm dissolved in 3 mL water.
